body:

[plonchi] Privacy-focused devices, encrypted, local storage and no subscription.
[klaw81] @Bretttick: Reolink, TP-Link and Eufy doorbells have a good feature set and decent performance for a reasonable price. They don't lock features behind subscription paywalls, they're designed to store data locally and can be isolated from the cloud.

[Juiici] I've got Wyze cams and they work well, relatively cheap subscription, and more responsive than Ring or Nest cams. I'll wait for someone to tell me they're a security concern too
[deebee8] because they require a subscription for any useful features. the only thing for free is notifications and live view. Getting a Tapo product is probably the best option for entry level, onsite storage and get most feature for free. Only cloud storage is paywalled IIRC.
[spackbace] H500 hub is a good option to unlock the features normally reserved for the cloud
[pinkybrain] @spackbace: does the H500 hub unlock rich text notification on Tapo cameras?
they normally lock in behind cloud subscription
[plonchi] Do you not watch the news?
you think its great having america company camera that have mass surveillance built in is a good idea when america collapsing and acting the way it is? You think ring cameras are a good idea if the king of America wants out resources and says fork it, Australia is ours now….
[netsurfer] Assuming you don't pay for the subscription (and frankly, if people are FOMO buying this, they won't), don't expect Ring / Amazon to spy on you for free.
The main issue with this is that the features are far more limited without subscription.
As for big brother watching… we all use phones running on an OS from an US company. If you use a "free" email service, chances are it is done by an American company and that company already scans all your emails. Our government knows your bank transactions. If you actually comment on OZB regularly, then honestly, you are not worth spying on.
[netsurfer] If you intend to use it as purely as a simple doorbell with basic video features (only able to capture people stay near the doorbell for long enough), then it is probably okay. Ring tries to hook you into their subscription model. No subscription means no saved recording.
If your Internet is down, then the doorbell is essentially a brick until Internet is up again.
[Thanks Purchased 8] Dont forget an annual subscription in that price
[Cludos] not needed if just use as a door bell and notification.
[geekcohen] These are probably being cleared out due to a new model.
[Cludos] $40 delivered a cheap door bell with notifications or not?
[McMaferMur] not due to Subscription.
Hey, maybe you are new to OzBargain, but not every cheap deal is worth buying. Sometimes you might think you really really really need and hey its cheap everyone else buying so why not?, but if you give it a week, you'll see that your life is totally fine without it. Plus, you'll have some extra cash saved for those rainy days.
[poppingtags] I've been using mine for years because I had a bunch of Echo devices, and it's worked exceptionally well without a subscription. I just need to know when someone rings the bell and I need to be able to talk through the doorbell even when I'm not at home. Works well for that.
[jimojr] I picked up a Blink Outdoor 4 camera system with a free video doorbell for just $35 on Prime Day. I use an Echo as the doorbell chime and record videos locally through the Sync Module 2, so there’s no subscription fee.
I’ve been using it for more than two months now and I’m really happy with it. The camera itself is still sitting in the box.
[MLP] Have had this doorbell for a while and it’s great. Can answer if not home and tell delivery person where to leave my parcel.
Subscription is $4.99 a month and you get a month free but I use it without the subscription. Only use subscription when I’m away on holidays (have a couple of cameras as well so subscription is $14.99 but can cancel before end of month and get balance refunded).
Debating buying this as a spare (the battery alone costs $49).
[pinkybrain] why not just get a tapo/reolink etc. which does not require subscription to get most of features that ring subscription offer?

I don’t think anyone will try rip it off
[JayParker] Which state are you in? Vic rental laws now allow tenant to male minor charges such as screwing things in without permission from landlord
[legionarypullo] I've found a different use case for these that might make them worthwhile for fellow OzBargainers. Specifically, these can be used, without a subscription, as:
-a smart button (e.g., use Alexa to set a routine to turn a light on when the doorbell button is pressed - making sure to turn off the doorbell sound)
-a sensor (e.g. turn a light on when movement is detected)
-a live view camera
-an intercom (you can talk to people from app).
Or you could use them as, well, doorbells, just without recording ability.
If you can get these cheap, they can be pretty useful!
Edit: The above use cases are more relevant to the hardwired ones (you can plug them ito a wall outlet) - not so much the battery version I guess.
[crentist] Good ideas. No reason the battery version wouldn't do all those, they are kinda the basic features of the video doorbell.
One extra detail - screws on the back can be hardwired to register button presses directly into other electronics. So it can also be a "dumb button".
The most basic application of this would be to wire it into an existing doorbell/intercom system. That way you don't need to completely replace an older system just to upgrade the doorbell.
[legionarypullo] That's really interesting about hardwiring to use as a dumb button… i'll look into it, thanks.
[sspal] Thanks for sharing. Already have 1 door bell but dont have the chime. Now use the chime and may be sell the door bell on marketplace . 😉
